name: story-architecture.template
notes: FORMAT EXAMPLE — NOT AN INSTRUMENT. This file exists to show the shape a W1 question set takes; the questions below are placeholders that demonstrate the three scale kinds, not proposed architecture questions. Every id is in the reserved `example_` namespace, and instrument.freeze() refuses that namespace, so this file cannot become a real instrument by accident. Choosing the ~30 real questions is the study's central scientific act and is gated on the human-agreement work in GENERATIVE-VARIANCE-PLAN.md §6.2-6.4 — it is not a tooling decision. To start a real one: copy this file, give it a distinct name, replace every question, and freeze it only once the questions are settled (§6.5: freezing is a one-way door, and changing a question after collection invalidates every trial already scored). Fields `notes` and per-question `note` are NOT hashed and stay editable after a freeze; `id`, `text`, `kind`, `lo`, `hi` and their ORDER are the instrument's identity.

questions.text: A graded judgement the scorer places on a fixed ordinal scale.
questions.note: The default shape. `lo`/`hi` are inclusive and a value outside them raises rather than being clipped — a scorer answering 7 on a 1-5 scale is a detectable failure, and clipping would hide it.

questions.text: A presence/absence judgement: is this structural feature there at all?
questions.note: 0 means the scorer answered 'no'. It does NOT mean the scorer declined — a declined question is omitted from the answers dict entirely and lands as NaN in the trial vector (§7).

questions.text: A proportion of the story, in [0, 1].
questions.note: Same numeric range as `binary` but a different quantity; the kind is recorded so a later reader is not left inferring it from the bounds.
